title: Soviet consulate Hakodate (Kiselev) and trade offices: five-digit-group cipher telegrams copied by the Hokkaido police, 'meaning unknown'
correspondents: Soviet consul at Hakodate (Kiselev) → Soviet embassy Tokyo and consulates; Soviet trade offices at Vladivostok / Harbin / Peking
shelfmark: JACAR B14090576500 (items 2, frames 394-400) and B14090579100 (vol. 2, frames 6-7), MOFA Diplomatic Archives, 在本邦各国公館関係雑件／蘇連邦ノ部／領事館及通商代表部状況雑報 (外甲秘 4471, 22 Oct 1929; 4776, 15 Nov 1929; 4799, 18 Nov 1929; 530, 8 Apr 1930; 14 Apr 1930)
folio_note: B14090576500: 7 frames, handwritten five-digit groups on ruled telegram forms, about 6 telegrams (frames 396-399); frame 400 has a column of Latin-letter pseudo-words. B14090579100 (83 frames): only frames 6-7 are telegram forms (10 and 15 Nov 1929, five-digit groups); the rest is Japanese report text, plans and photographs, all viewed on a contact sheet. About 8 telegrams in all
status: Hokkaido governor's cover letters to the Home and Foreign Ministers say the consul sent cipher telegrams 'of unknown meaning' from the Hakodate post office; the groups are copied out. No key, no decipherment, no Japanese reading in the file. Not on DECODE (checked 27 Oct 2026). The Japanese Army obtained a Soviet trade-mission code in Sept 1933 (C01004002600, 155 frames) which may belong to the same family: key lead, not yet looked at
why: A Soviet consul's cipher traffic in Japan at the start of the 1929-30 trade and fishery disputes: a rare original ciphertext of Soviet diplomatic five-figure code from the interwar period, with dates and senders known
score_note: Scored from the images (frames 394-400 viewed 27 Oct 2026, research/jacar/): short, no key, probably an additive-enciphered code
verify: Transcribe the groups from the PDF (JACAR /das/image/B14090576500, 7 pages), test for a 5-digit code with 2-digit additive; compare with the code in C01004002600 (frames 395 onward) and with other Soviet 5-digit traffic

title: Army General Staff telegrams in cipher with Lt-Gen Yamaguchi and Maj-Gen Fukushima in China, 1901 (Boxer aftermath): five-digit groups with enciphered romanised words
correspondents: Lt-Gen Yamaguchi / Tamura ↔ Maj-Gen Fukushima (Army General Staff, Tokyo)
folio_note: 5 records of 2-3 frames each, about 73 code groups in all (5, 6, 24, 30, 8). Each telegram mixes five-digit code groups with Latin-letter strings that look like enciphered romaji ('kotowaina', 'ikaga', 'Kitawrnozomio'). The clear telegram of 8 Mar 1901 (C09122810200, request for 10,000 yen more secret funds) is in the same volume: possible crib for C09122810100
status: Transcribed in the JACAR record text but no decipherment, key or Japanese reading in the volume (pages viewed 27 Oct 2026). Not on DECODE. Not checked against published work on Meiji army codes
why: The Army General Staff's own cipher in the year after the Boxer expedition, in what looks like a hybrid of a numeric code book and enciphered romanised kana: an early Japanese military cipher with no known key
score_note: Scored from the images and descriptions during the Oct 2026 JACAR sweep (research/jacar/); only C09122810100 viewed in full
verify: Transcribe the 73 groups and strings from the JACAR PDFs; test whether the Latin strings are a substitution over romanised Japanese (word lengths, 'ikaga', 'tegai'); compare the 8 Mar telegram with C09122810200

title: Japanese Navy numeral telegram to HMS Newcastle sent by Otoshi and Yokosuka radio stations, 38 five-digit groups
correspondents: Navy Ministry adjutant (Otoshi/Yokosuka radio) → British cruiser HMS Newcastle
shelfmark: JACAR C11080235200; 防衛省防衛研究所, 海軍省-武往文-T-6-28, 日英海軍交渉関係書類 大正3年8月~大正6年1月
folio_note: 2 frames; 38 five-digit groups in the record text
status: The record text gives the instruction to pass 'a numeral telegram' to Newcastle and then the groups. No key; likely a Royal Navy or joint Anglo-Japanese code, which would be outside this repository. Not viewed, not on DECODE
why: A numeral cipher passed between the Japanese and British navies in the first month of the First World War; short, so mostly a lead for the Anglo-Japanese naval files
score_note: Scored from the JACAR record text during the Oct 2026 JACAR sweep (research/jacar/); images not viewed
verify: View the 2 frames; look for the sibling records in 日英海軍交渉関係書類 for the matching reply or plain text
